cleanIntro: The Octane 9 is designed to be stripped and cleaned by its owner, and SilencerCo says so on the page. It is a pistol can that gets shot wet as well as dry, so the interval is not a round count — it is whenever it has been used wet, and at regular intervals otherwise. ⛔ The aluminum tube gets completely different treatment from the baffles: the serial number is on it.

steps.title: Firearm unloaded and the action OPEN before the can moves
steps.action: Open the action and see that the firearm is visibly clear of ammunition — before the silencer goes on and before it comes off. A suppressed gun is quieter, not safer, and the book says so in as many words.
steps.quote: Before installing the silencer on the host firearm, be sure that the firearm is unloaded and the action is opened so that the firearm is visibly clear of any ammunition.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Octane Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. It prints "2.0" zero times. — WARNING

steps.title: ⛔ NO GAP at the shoulder — check the fit before firing
steps.action: This is the check that prevents a baffle strike. The thread mount must be FULLY shouldered against the barrel with no visible gap between the barrel shoulder and the face of the mount. If there is a gap, the silencer does not go on the gun that day.
steps.aside: Silencers must be free of obstructions such as mud, dirt, etc. DO NOT attempt to shoot through an obstructed silencer.
steps.quote: The thread mount must be fully shouldered on the barrel. There should be no visible gap between the barrel shoulder and the face of the silencer thread mount.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Octane Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. It prints "2.0" zero times. — WARNING

steps.title: ⛔ Re-check tightness every 30 rounds
steps.action: Silencers back off under recoil, and a partly-unthreaded can is how baffle strikes happen. SilencerCo names an interval rather than leaving it to feel: verify the attachment is secure after about 30 discharges.
steps.quote: To ensure your silencer remains secure while firing, it is of the utmost importance that you frequently verify the silencer is securely tightened onto the barrel. We recommend checking the security of the attachment after 30 discharges of the firearm.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Octane Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. It prints "2.0" zero times. — WARNING

steps.title: Front cap off, baffle stack out
steps.action: Take the front cap off — the sprocketed end of the piston is the tool, and a screwdriver through the piston holes gives you leverage if it is tight. The baffle stack and its expansion chamber slide out of the tube. Disassembly is the assembly steps in reverse.
steps.aside: To disassemble, perform steps in reverse order.
steps.quote: Twist front cap onto silencer; hand tighten with the sprocketed end of piston. For extra leverage, insert a screwdriver through piston holes and twist.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Octane Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. It prints "2.0" zero times. — Assembly & Disassembly

steps.title: Piston assembly out of the rear
steps.action: The piston assembly comes out of the back of the silencer with its spring — or, on a fixed-barrel host, a fixed barrel spacer in place of the spring — seated in the spring retainer.
steps.quote: Place spring or fixed barrel spacer over piston and seat into spring retainer. Insert the assembly into the rear of the silencer; tighten until securely seated.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Octane Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. It prints "2.0" zero times. — Piston Mount

steps.title: Clean at intervals — and always after shooting WET
steps.action: SilencerCo asks for the silencer and its individual components to be disassembled and cleaned at regular intervals, and specifically whenever it has been shot "wet" — that is, with 5cc or less of water or lubricant put inside to cool the gases.
steps.aside: The Octane is designed to be easily maintained by the user.
steps.quote: It is recommended that the silencer and its individual components be disassembled and cleaned at regular intervals, or whenever the silencer is shot “wet”.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Octane Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. It prints "2.0" zero times. — Maintenance

steps.title: ⛔ The aluminum tube is NOT the baffles — and the serial is on it
steps.action: The aluminum tube, the front cap and the spring retainer must not be soaked in chemicals or put in an ultrasonic cleaner. Two reasons, and SilencerCo gives both: the finish, and the fact that the chemicals can react with the aluminum and ERASE THE SERIAL NUMBER. Damp cloth or a non-abrasive brush, gently.
steps.aside: The aluminum tube, front cap, and spring retainer should NOT be soaked in chemicals or used in an ultrasonic cleaner due to the potential for damage to the finish and the potential to erase the serial number due reaction with the aluminum tube.
steps.quote: We recommend using a damp cloth or non-abrasive brush to gently wipe or scrub away debris.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Octane Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. It prints "2.0" zero times. — OUTER TUBE

steps.title: Baffles: solvent, nylon brush, time — no metal scrapers
steps.action: Gun solvents and CLP break the fouling up; a nylon brush, cotton buds and rags do the rest, and it is mostly patience. ⛔ Never use hard metal tools to scrape lead and carbon off — you will damage the metal, and the lead you are scraping is its own hazard.
steps.aside: Dry all components thoroughly before reassembling.
steps.quote: Don't use hard metal tools to scrape lead and carbon off your components as you may damage the metal.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Octane Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. It prints "2.0" zero times. — SCRUBBING

deepAbsentReason: SilencerCo publishes ONE level of disassembly for this silencer and it is the routine cleaning itself — the strip in the Assembly & Disassembly section is what an owner does every cleaning interval, not an occasional deep service. There is nothing deeper published, and nothing was borrowed: the SEALED SilencerCo cans in this same batch publish LESS, not more, so there is no sibling to take a deeper procedure from even if one were wanted.

cleaning.name: BAFFLES
tasks: Gun solvent or CLP to break the fouling up
Nylon brush, cotton buds, rags — patience rather than force
Dry thoroughly; oil them after a water-based cleaner

cleaning.name: ⛔ ALUMINIUM TUBE, FRONT CAP, SPRING RETAINER
tasks: ⛔ NOT soaked in chemicals, NOT ultrasonic — it can erase the serial
Damp cloth or non-abrasive brush, gently

cleaning.name: PISTON ASSEMBLY
tasks: Out of the rear with its spring or fixed-barrel spacer
Carbon off the piston and the retainer

cleaning.name: AFTER SHOOTING WET
tasks: Strip and clean it — do not leave water or lubricant inside

reassembly: Baffles aligned facing the same way and clicked together into a stack — all identical.
Alignment marks on the outsides used so the cutouts orient properly.
Expansion chamber snapped onto the CONE end (not the flat end), internal ridge closest to the cone.
Stack slid in expansion-chamber-first until it stops against the piston housing.
Front cap twisted on and hand tightened with the sprocketed end of the piston.
Piston assembly with spring (or fixed barrel spacer) seated into the spring retainer and tightened into the rear.
